identity.description: Squarespace is a website builder and ecommerce platform. The Squarespace Developer Platform at developers.squarespace.com documents its Commerce APIs, Reseller APIs, Custom Code Spec, OAuth and an MCP server.
identity.identity_notes: The developer portal describes Squarespace's Commerce, Reseller and Custom Code APIs, and it points to the Squarespace account developer-apps page. The product matches the assignment.

auth.oauth_flows: Authorization code flow. Authorize at /authorize with access_type=offline for long-term access, then exchange the code at POST https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/tokens. Authorization codes last 2 minutes and are single-use.
auth.token_refresh: Access tokens last 30 minutes. Refresh tokens last 7 days and are one-time use: the old refresh token is invalidated when a new access token is used. API keys do not expire while the merchant site remains active.
auth.scopes_notes: OAuth scopes include website.orders(.read), website.transactions.read, website.inventory(.read), website.products(.read), website.contacts(.read), website.discounts(.read). API keys are granted per API with Read Only or Read and Write permission, and the permissions cannot be changed later. Webhook Subscriptions require OAuth. Keys are sent as a Bearer value in the Authorization header, with a User-Agent header. Plain HTTP is rejected.

access.production_restrictions: OAuth client registration is reviewed by Squarespace before client_id/client_secret are issued. Custom apps for a merchant site need the Commerce Advanced plan. API keys are generated by the site owner in Settings > Advanced > Developer API Keys, so the merchant must do this. Keys and tokens only reach the site that owns them.

read_ops: Get address book and address book entry
Read orders, products, inventory, transactions (per Commerce APIs overview)
write_ops: Create, replace and delete address book entries
Write orders, products, inventory (per Commerce APIs overview; exact endpoints not confirmed)
api.limitations: Coverage is Commerce-focused. Other areas (Domains, Reseller, Custom Code) are separate programs. Rate limits and sandbox are not documented on the pages checked. Webhook Subscriptions are listed as OAuth only. The official sites show code samples in many languages but no official SDK is named.

open_questions: Conflict: the search snippet of the authentication page says 'Squarespace Extensions are required to use OAuth', but the OAuth page says Extensions are not required. Verify on the live pages.

The paid-plan requirement for API keys comes from a search summary and a third-party guide (StackOne). The official auth page only names Commerce Advanced for custom applications. Confirm which plan (Commerce Basic/Advanced) is needed for keys.
Rate limits, sandbox or test sites, and free trial availability are not documented on the pages checked.
The webhook topics list, signature scheme, and retry behavior were not retrieved. The /commerce-apis/webhooks page returned 404.
Full write-operation list for orders, products and inventory was not confirmed at endpoint level.
Official MCP server: the repo is not named, and the server's client list (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) comes from the MCP overview page only. Commerce tools are described as read-only for orders.

Community MCP servers were only seen in search results (GitHub BusyBee3333 repo, Glama, LobeHub, a Python squarespace-mcp package, Zapier/StackOne/MCPBundles hosted connectors). None was opened or verified.
Some Squarespace MCP features may not match the public API, according to a GitHub issue on anthropics/claude-ai-mcp. That issue was not opened.

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Production/public use requires vendor app review.
